attribution.note: Marcus's own bullet in his own post, stated as fact.

semantics.note: Factual observation that Oracle debt was downgraded. The 'ominous sign' framing is correctly left unscored.

contract.note: Marcus did not say who downgraded. Counting a major bank's credit research cut to Underweight as a debt downgrade is an ordinary reading; it was widely reported that way. A strict agency-only reading would give a different result, so interpretation matters.

evidence.note: Secondary report that Barclays credit analyst cut Oracle debt to Underweight on Nov 11, 2025, inside the target window.
Dates the Barclays fixed income report to Nov 11 and gives its AI-capex rationale.
Shows this was an analyst recommendation that anticipated an agency cut, not an agency rating action.

reviews.rationale: On the contract's fair plain reading, Barclays' credit research downgrade of Oracle debt to Underweight on Nov 11, 2025 meets the support condition. The packet shows no agency downgrade in the window; the caveat is that the evidence is secondary coverage dated the same day as the post.

attribution.note: Marcus's own bullet in his own post.

semantics.note: Observation about what Altman said. 'Couldn't explain' is partly a judgment about whether his explanation was adequate.

contract.note: The result depends on whether 'couldn't explain' means no explanation at all or no convincing one. Marcus set no standard. Which appearance he meant (BG2 or general) is also unclear.

evidence.note: On BG2, Altman got defensive when asked about $1.4T and deflected with an offer to find a buyer for the host's shares.
In his Nov 6 X post, Altman set out a revenue path: above $20B run rate, hundreds of billions by 2030, against $1.4T over 8 years.
The same post named equity and debt, plus new business lines, as funding sources.
Even on BG2 he pointed to revenue growth, though without specifics.

reviews.rationale: Part holds: on BG2 Altman deflected and gave no concrete account. Part fails: before the post, his Nov 6 X post laid out a funding path (revenue growth, new lines, equity, debt), so the literal 'gave no explanation' reading is contradicted. Whether that path was adequate cannot be scored.

semantics.note: Observation: a roughly 20% weekly fall in CRWV shares. The framing is not scored.

contract.note: Reading it as a roughly 20% fall over a recent trading week is ordinary and fair.

evidence.note: Motley Fool reports CRWV fell 22.2% in the trading week ending Nov 7, 2025.

reviews.rationale: A financial news report shows CRWV fell 22.2% in the week ending Nov 7, 2025, just before the post. That meets the roughly 20% weekly drop. The packet has no conflicting price data.

attribution.note: Marcus's own bullet in his own post.

semantics.note: Factual claim that SoftBank sold its entire Nvidia stake. The 'ominous' framing is not scored.

contract.note: The plain reading (all Nvidia shares sold, including by SB Northstar) is fair.

evidence.note: SoftBank's own Nov 11 investor briefing says sale of all shares held was completed in Oct, covering SBG and SB Northstar. This is a company disclosure.
Tom's Hardware independently reports the full exit: 32.1M shares for $5.83B in October.
CFO's reason (funding OpenAI) bears only on the framing, not on whether the sale happened.

reviews.rationale: SoftBank's disclosure and contemporaneous news coverage both show SoftBank sold all its Nvidia shares in October 2025, disclosed on Nov 11. That matches the claim.
